title: Calif publishes one-click chain that leaked Tor Browser users' real IP; Privacy Affairs says part of the fix never reached the older Tor Browser branch
date_note: Privacy Affairs (published 27 November) says Calif published its research on 26 November; Calif's own page was not read.
geo_basis: no place stated; a browser flaw
summary: Privacy Affairs reports that security firm Calif published a chain in which one click on a malicious page revealed the real IP of Tor Browser 15.0.22 users on Linux. Calif says the chain stopped working in 15.0.23. Privacy Affairs says, from public code, that the older Tor Browser branch never received a second fix, and says it has asked the Tor Project and Mozilla about this. Mozilla's advisory rates the Streams use-after-free CVE-2026-92027 high.
plain: Privacy Affairs reports researchers showed one click on a booby-trapped page could expose a Tor Browser user's real IP address. Calif says the chain stopped working in 15.0.23.
exec: Privacy Affairs reports a published attack chain could unmask Tor Browser users; it says the older Tor Browser branch never got one of the two fixes.
action: General advice: update Tor Browser to the current release; Privacy Affairs notes Tor Browser 16.0.3 is current and that Calif says the chain stopped working in 15.0.23.

validation.note: Only Privacy Affairs describes the one-click chain; Mozilla's advisory was read for CVE-2026-92027 only. Calif's write-up, the Tor Project and the second fix were not read.
